facts.advisory_summary:

When the `register_argc_argv php` directive is set to `on` , and users call any URL with a special crafted query string, they are able to change the environment used by the framework when handling the request.

The framework now ignores argv values for environment detection on non-cli SAPIs.

Koel documents no PHP runtime/php.ini settings for production; docs/guide/getting-started.md:60-66 says `php artisan serve` is only the development server and production should be nginx/Apache pointed at public/ (nginx.conf.example:4,34 is php-fpm via fastcgi, no PHP_VALUE override). The official Docker image is in a separate repo and not documented here. facts.advisory_summary:
Symfony's incorrect argument escaping under MSYS2/Git Bash can lead to destructive file operations on Windows — ### Summary
The Symfony Process component did not correctly treat some characters (notably `=`) as “special” when escaping arguments on Windows. When PHP is executed from an MSYS2-based environment (e.g. Git Bash) and Symfony Process spawns native Windows executables, MSYS2’s argument/path conversion can mishandle unquoted arguments containing these characters.

This can cause the spawned process to receive corrupted/truncated arguments compared to what Symfony intended.

### Impact

expect.note: Only affects PHP running under MSYS2/Git Bash on Windows spawning native executables; not a documented deployment (Koel uses Process for ffmpeg transcoding app/Values/TranscodeResult.php:33 on a web server).

zbateson/mail-mime-parser has uncontrolled resource consumption (CPU/memory DoS) parsing untrusted MIME — ### Impact

An uncontrolled resource consumption / algorithmic complexity vulnerability affecting any application that parses untrusted email with this library.

Three independent parsing paths are super-linear in cost, so a byte-size cap on the caller side does **not** bound the work done.  A crafted message under 2 MB can consume seconds of CPU or hundreds of megabytes to multiple gigabytes of memory (leading to an out-of-memory kill), enabling denial of service. Any log message containing 'Message-ID' and 'To:' is parsed by MailMimeParser (LoggedMailPayload.php:36) before Ray's enabled check.
